findings.reason: it adds the residue ruling §3/§4/§5 already have (carry the existing kernel into `topology.read` as a private helper, or state why it fails the traced fixed-shape contract), which changes §2's node scope and forces §6 to say whether `contour_tree.py` is retained or deleted.
findings.text: §2 requires implementing the contour-tree authority on hex cells but carries no reuse ruling for `contour_tree.build_contour_tree` (nova/equilibrium/contour_tree.py:384) and `contour_tree_mesh.build_contour_mesh` (nova/equilibrium/contour_tree_mesh.py:193) — a traced, fixed-capacity, deterministic-tie-ordering contour-tree builder and its wall-clipped hex-carrier triangulation, which is precisely §2's stated contract ("contour-tree authority on hex cells", "pure, traced", "fixed-capacity buffers"); `stencil_nulls.py`'s `critical_point_candidates_batch`/`xpoint_candidates`/`magnetic_axis_subgrid` (a quadratic-fit stationary-point evaluator, production-reachable via `profile.py` and `connectivity_boundary.py`) is likewise unnamed. §2 currently names only the `nova/biot` null kernels, so the §2 node would rebuild a kernel the tree already contains

findings.reason: it names the owner to extend rather than fork, the same rule the plan already applied to `nova/biot/null.py`; forking a second contour-tree reader splits the authority the lead locked (contour tree on hex cells) across two implementations that will drift, and §6 must then reconcile which one the retirement leaves standing.
findings.text: the contour-tree authority §2 proposes has an existing owner: `build_contour_tree(vertex_psi, vertex_valid, vertex_is_wall, edges, edge_valid, sigma)` already builds a fixed-capacity contour tree whose join/split sweeps are traceable through `jax.jit` and `jax.vmap` with deterministic vertex-index tie ordering, and `contour_tree_mesh.build_contour_mesh` already builds the clipped hex-centre triangulation carrying it; today its only non-test importer is `nova/imas/contour_tree_layout.py`, so it is an exercised kernel awaiting an equilibrium caller, not a competing implementation

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the four proposed entry points (`topology.read`, `current.book`, `gs.apply`, `solve.fixed_point`) each hide an entire subsystem behind one call, replacing the 54,102-line sprawl rather than spreading it across shallow wrappers; §1's landed design and §5's single-`ladder.scan`-site contract carry that intent.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §2 would build a second contour-tree authority beside `nova/equilibrium/contour_tree.py`, which already owns one.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — the supplied counts are public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §2 and §5 each state their new policy type is carried by the existing `ForwardSolvePolicy` "extended rather than duplicated" (a named merge), and §6 names the routes, ladders, frozen/live split and owners it retires, so no adding section leaves its surface unaccounted for.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §2 ("the contour tree on hex cells") is the only implementation section with no cite-or-justify reuse ruling, and it builds a mechanism the codebase already owns a traced kernel for.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — every section replaces its predecessor rather than layering on it (§4 states "`gs.apply` replaces the map `ForwardFluxOperator` performs today rather than wrapping it"; §2/§3/§5 each name the modules replaced, and §6 deletes them), so no wrapper is added over machinery that could have been extended.
